answer: The opal multiplier is published, charged in thread, and jade lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3036 identities would post 4117 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
